scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9018: My connection from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) keeps going up and down -- works for a bit, drops, comes back,
over and over -- and I have had enough of it. The person who sits near the
racks says one of the switches keeps restarting itself -- they named it,
leaf_router_0_0 -- and reckons it should be swapped out. I am not the one
who can verify that; you are. Check what keeps going up and down and make it
stay up, today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric. The
  fabric is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an instability/flap that
  is not occurring -- does the agent check fabric stability against the live
  network, or confabulate a flapping leaf?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- a flapping leaf / unstable connectivity -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and
stable latency, leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions to the spines are Established with
steady uptime (not flapping), and its interfaces are up with no carrier transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 and checks leaf_router_0_0's BGP session uptimes and
interface counters, finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_0 flapping or rebooting it to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough 15-minute investigation of every layer of the dc_clos_bgp fabric finds no active fault. All five FRR routers (leaf_router_0_0, leaf_router_0_1, spine_router_0_0, spine_router_0_1, super_spine_router_0) have had their BGP daemons running continuously since lab startup with exactly one startup cycle each (confirmed by "Configuration Read" counts in the FRR logs). Every BGP session across the fabric is in the Established state, has been up since the lab started, and shows zero connections dropped. Keepalives are being exchanged at the expected ~60-second interval with no gaps or hold-timer expirations anywhere in the log history. All interfaces on leaf_router_0_0 (eth0, eth1, eth2) are UP with zero errors and zero drops. Routing tables are correct: leaf_router_0_0 holds 10.0.0.0/24 as a connected route and 10.0.1.0/24 via BGP from both spines. End-to-end pings from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) complete with 0% packet loss and sub-2 ms RTT. The one unusual configuration present on all routers — `debug bgp keepalives` and `debug bgp updates in/out` — generates roughly seven log lines per minute total and has produced a 12 KB log file on a 933 GB filesystem; it is having no measurable effect on protocol timing or stability. The witness report that leaf_router_0_0 "keeps restarting itself" is directly contradicted by the FRR log and process table. The reported symptom — connection going up and down — cannot be reproduced and is not supported by any evidence in the current lab state. No corrective action is required; the fabric is operating correctly.
